subject: Sandbox routing & conditional TIA proposal for Acme Health
messages:
From: Martin Renshaw <martin.r@acmehealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>, Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial question: sandbox dev teams & EU data flow

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. A quick follow-up from our security team: our EU clinical sandbox environments are occasionally accessed by APAC dev teams for analytics experiments. We need to understand whether Redwood's routing (hosted + dedicated fallbacks) would cause EU-origin session data to be processed outside the EEA in those cases, and what legal mechanisms you rely on (SCCs, UK IDTA + addendum, TIA/DTIA findings).

Specific asks:
- Can you confirm the default routing behavior when a request comes from a European patient dataset and the nearest capacity is an APAC instance?
- Do you have a standard Transfer Impact Assessment and an evidence package we can review (subprocessors, logs, KV cache residency)?
- We're also interested in whether a conditional approach (e.g., allow sandbox dev access only under an approved subprocessor attestation) is something Redwood supports.

If possible, please attach a short mapping matrix and any sample redlines to the UK IDTA. We need the materials to feed our DPA review meeting next Tuesday.

Best,
Martin
Martin Renshaw
Head of Security Operations — Acme Health

Attachments: none

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial question: sandbox dev teams & EU data flow

Martin,

Appreciate the clear asks — I'm looping in Kimberly (legal) and Laura (privacy/eng) to make sure you have both the legal and operational answers. High level answers up front:

- Routing: by default we route to nearest compatible capacity by region policy, but customers can pin residency (hosted routing policies) or require on-prem / VPC-only processing. When pinned to EU, we ensure session and KV cache residency stays in-region; fallbacks only occur to compatible EU variants unless customer permits cross-region fallback.
- Legal mechanisms: we support SCCs (as a baseline), we maintain a UK IDTA with a customer-facing addendum for UK-data-specific requirements, and we produce a TIA/DTIA for higher-risk use cases. We can provide a summary TIA and the subprocessor registry excerpt for your review.
- Conditional sandbox access: yes, we can gate sandbox access by subprocessor attestations or by whitelisting dev identities tied to approved regions. We typically implement this as an access policy + routing rule and record the change in the audit log.

I've attached a compact transfer matrix and a starter UK IDTA redline for your team to review. Laura will follow up with details on the DTIA/TIA artifacts we can share under NDA.

Next steps proposed:
1) I will send the transfer matrix (attached) and a short TIA executive summary.
2) Kimberly will confirm what changes we can accept in the UK addendum and any negotiation constraints.
3) If helpful, we can run a short workflow demo (15 mins) showing a sandbox failover to an APAC dev node and the resulting logs.

Do any of those work for your Tuesday DPA meeting?

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Head of Compliance — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-transfer-matrix-v1.xlsx, uk-idta-draft-redlines.docx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial question: sandbox dev teams & EU data flow

Martin / team,

Following up on legal constraints and pragmatic positions:

- UK IDTA: we can accept targeted, limited redlines that clarify the subprocessor notice periods and the evidence delivery cadence (e.g., 30 days for attestation updates). We cannot accept redlines that change core liability caps in the master DPA.
- SCCs/Transfers: SCCs are our baseline international transfer mechanism for hosted customers. For customers that require stronger controls, we offer an IDTA/UK addendum package plus a TIA that documents residual risks and mitigations (encryption-in-transit, geo-routing, cache eviction policies).
- DTIA artifacts we can share: redacted TIA summary, subprocessor registry snapshot, sample KV residency logs (redacted). Full TIA PDFs are available under NDA.

Operational ask: we need Acme to identify the specific sandbox projects and the APAC teams that will access them. That lets us scope the TIA and produce a short conditional access policy.

Quick note on timelines: if you need materials for Tuesday's DPA meeting, we can provide the transfer matrix and a two-page TIA executive summary by EOD tomorrow (Thu). The UK IDTA redline commentary will follow early next week.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection

Subject: Re: Initial question: sandbox dev teams & EU data flow

Martin,

Following Kimberly's note, a few engineering/ops details to help you assess the residual risk in a sandbox scenario:

- Cache & Session residency: when a workspace is pinned to EU, the KV cache writes are routed to EU-only nodes. We perform automated cache eviction on region-change and provide audit logs showing the node IDs handling sessions. The logs we can share will be redacted to remove customer-identifying tokens.
- Failover behavior: if EU capacity is exhausted and you allow multi-region failover, we only route to certified regions listed in the TIA (we won't arbitrarily route to any APAC region). You can pick a policy of "no cross-border failover" for sandbox environments if desired.
- Subprocessor conditionality: we support conditional access via a combination of (1) subprocessor attestation required before dev access, (2) a routing label on the request that enforces region, and (3) audit webhook that flags any cross-region processing attempts.

I uploaded a redacted sample of the KV-residency log and a short op playbook to the Drive link below. Those should help your ops folks understand what to expect in the audit.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c4TiaPlaybook

Action items for Acme: please send a list of sandbox project names + dev team emails and confirm whether "no cross-border failover" is a hard requirement. If it is, we'll prepare a scoped addendum and a canary test plan.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Privacy Engineering
Redwood Inference

Summary of position:
- Redwood will provide: (a) transfer matrix (attached), (b) a two-page TIA executive summary (attached as PDF under NDA), and (c) a redacted subprocessor registry snapshot.
- UK IDTA redline: Redwood legal will provide commentary on the draft redlines; we can accept language that clarifies notice windows and evidence cadence but cannot change liability caps.
- Sandbox routing: Acme can choose "no cross-border failover" for the named sandbox projects. If chosen, Redwood will enforce the routing label and run a canary test showing no cross-border session handling.
- Conditional access: we will enable a subprocessor-attestation gating flow for the dev identities you list.

Deliverables & timeline:
1) Transfer matrix & TIA executive summary — EOD Thu (attachment: redwood-transfer-matrix-v1.xlsx; acme-tia-questionnaire.pdf).
2) UK IDTA redline commentary — by Mon next week. (attachment: uk-idta-draft-redlines.docx)
3) Canary test & demo — schedule a 15-min session; ops will own the runbook.
